intent.statement: A macOS user can leave Disk Steward running as a lightweight menu-bar app, understand material disk growth, export trustworthy evidence for Codex or Claude, and query the same evidence through a read-only local MCP integration.

success_evidence.description: A signed-development build launches as a menu-bar utility; left-click opens a compact status board and right-click exposes Export, Settings, About, and Quit.
The app measures whole-volume capacity while collecting bounded detailed evidence for configured roots and registered agent process trees.
Evidence identifies path, time, size delta, actor and agent session when observable, and labels exact, tool-linked, inferred, or unknown attribution without guessing.
A user can export a portable, integrity-manifested evidence bundle containing a concise Codex brief and machine-readable detailed records.
Codex and Claude can query sanitized evidence through the same read-only local MCP executable without rescanning the disk.
Monitoring remains useful without restricted privileges and enables exact Endpoint Security provenance only when entitlement and user authorization are available.
The app records no file contents, provides explicit privacy exclusions and retention limits, and performs no deletion or cleanup mutation in this intent.
Automated and reproducible checks demonstrate buildability, evidence correctness, regression safety, bounded idle resource use, and recovery from unavailable monitoring components.

constraints: Use a native Swift-first macOS architecture and keep the continuously running footprint bounded.
Prefer macOS 13 or newer, Swift 6, AppKit for status-item mouse behavior, SwiftUI for presented UI, SQLite for local evidence, and the official Swift MCP SDK.
Treat Endpoint Security entitlement approval as an external dependency and preserve a functional FSEvents/snapshot fallback.
Keep MCP read-only and avoid an externally reachable HTTP listener.
Do not persist file contents, secrets, or unbounded raw write-event streams.
Every attribution statement must carry method and confidence.
Generated evidence and databases must have deterministic retention and size controls.
non_goals: Automatic deletion, cache purging, process termination, or destructive MCP tools.
Cloud synchronization, accounts, telemetry, or a hosted backend.
Detailed monitoring of external, network, Time Machine, or cloud-placeholder volumes by default.
Guaranteeing Apple Endpoint Security entitlement approval.

assumptions.statement: The development machine has a compatible Xcode and Swift toolchain for a macOS 13+ Swift 6 application.
A native project layout can package the menu app, a local MCP executable, and later a system extension without introducing a second application language.
Endpoint Security entitlement may be unavailable or delayed, so exact system-wide attribution cannot be a prerequisite for the standard product path.
A stdio MCP executable can serve both Codex and Claude while delegating sanitized queries to the local app-owned evidence service.

decisions.question: What is the smallest honest delivery ladder from an empty repository?
decisions.choice: Deliver four cumulative runnable increments: snapshot/export menu app; persistent evidence recorder; agent-queryable MCP integration; advanced exact provenance with fallback.
alternatives: Treat project scaffolding as an increment
decisions.rationale: Each selected rung gives the user a launchable, meaningful scenario and isolates storage, integration, and restricted-entitlement risks behind independent gates.

decisions.question: Which application stack should be primary?
decisions.choice: Swift 6 with a small AppKit NSStatusItem shell, SwiftUI presentation, a shared Swift core, and SQLite persistence.
alternatives: Tauri with a Rust core and web UI
Pure MenuBarExtra without AppKit status-item event handling
decisions.rationale: The selected stack directly accesses macOS monitoring, service-management, signing, and menu APIs while minimizing continuous runtime and cross-language boundaries.

decisions.question: How broadly should monitoring persist detailed evidence?
decisions.choice: Track whole-volume capacity everywhere accessible, but persist detailed evidence only for configured roots, registered agent process trees, and bounded investigation windows.
alternatives: Scan the whole disk only when asked
decisions.rationale: The hybrid model preserves unexplained-growth detection and agent attribution without creating an unbounded privacy and resource burden.

decisions.question: How should Codex and Claude access evidence?
decisions.choice: Bundle one read-only Swift MCP stdio executable that delegates to the app-owned evidence service over a protected local IPC boundary.
alternatives: Expose a persistent localhost HTTP server
Give each agent direct SQLite access
Maintain separate Codex and Claude implementations
decisions.rationale: One connector minimizes duplication and attack surface while keeping database ownership, sanitization, and retention inside the application.

decisions.question: How should exact system-wide attribution depend on Endpoint Security?
decisions.choice: Implement it as an advanced capability with explicit confidence semantics and retain a useful FSEvents/snapshot fallback.
alternatives: Block the whole product on entitlement approval
decisions.rationale: Entitlement approval is external and cannot be guaranteed; the product must remain honest and useful in its absence.

decisions.question: Should the first product intent perform cleanup?
decisions.choice: No; it will explain, export, and recommend while all MCP tools remain read-only.
decisions.rationale: Evidence trust and attribution accuracy must be established before introducing destructive operations.

nodes.title: Persistent bounded evidence recorder

nodes.title: Launchable disk snapshot and export utility

nodes.title: Validate native toolchain and packaging path

acceptance_criteria.description: A checked-in decision record identifies observed tool versions, minimum target, project layout, dependency strategy, build commands, and unavailable prerequisites without inventing them.

nodes.title: Define core evidence and privacy contracts

acceptance_criteria.description: Versioned contracts cover timestamps, paths, size deltas, actors, sessions, confidence/method, sanitization, retention, integrity, error states, and schema compatibility with executable fixtures.

required_evidence.description: JSON fixtures and tests reject missing confidence, unbounded retention, file contents, and malformed export manifests.

nodes.title: Create the native project foundation

acceptance_criteria.description: A clean checkout resolves dependencies and builds the empty application and test targets with one documented command.

required_evidence.description: Dependency resolution, debug build, and empty test-suite output from the documented environment.

nodes.title: Implement volume snapshot and basic export
nodes.summary: Read accessible local volume capacity through native APIs, represent it with the evidence contract, and export a deterministic current-snapshot bundle.

acceptance_criteria.description: The core reports nonnegative total, used, and available capacity for a fixture and the current data volume, and exports schema-valid JSON plus a concise brief without file contents.

required_evidence.description: Deterministic fixture tests, live smoke test, schema validation, and export manifest verification.

nodes.title: Implement menu-bar shell and compact status board
nodes.summary: Build an NSStatusItem shell with left-click SwiftUI popover, right-click utility menu, real snapshot display, export action, settings, about, and quit behavior.

acceptance_criteria.description: Left-click and right-click produce their distinct required surfaces, snapshot data is accessible, export is reachable, and the app does not require a Dock presence during normal operation.

required_evidence.description: Automated view-model/state tests plus reproducible launch and interaction observations with accessibility labels.

nodes.title: Audit launchable snapshot increment
nodes.summary: Independently verify build, launch, left/right-click UX, real capacity display, safe snapshot export, and reproduction instructions.

acceptance_criteria.description: A fresh build launches and completes the snapshot/export human journey; automated tests and schema checks pass; no content or destructive function is present.

required_evidence.description: Build/test logs, launch observation, interaction checklist, rendered popover evidence, and inspected export fixture.

nodes.title: Implement bounded SQLite evidence store
nodes.summary: Persist normalized snapshots and aggregated events with migrations, WAL-safe access, retention, compaction, integrity checks, and deterministic test clocks.

acceptance_criteria.description: Concurrent read/write fixtures preserve committed evidence, retention and aggregation bound growth, interrupted writes recover, and backup/export snapshots remain consistent.

required_evidence.description: Migration, concurrency, retention, compaction, backup, corruption-detection, and recovery test output.

nodes.title: Implement hybrid monitoring and growth explanation
nodes.summary: Collect whole-volume metrics and FSEvents-backed targeted changes, dynamically include registered roots, coalesce writes, detect unexplained growth, and produce confidence-labelled explanations.

acceptance_criteria.description: Fixture growth inside and outside watched roots yields bounded detailed or unexplained evidence as appropriate; exclusions, unavailable paths, event gaps, and investigation windows are explicit.

required_evidence.description: Deterministic collector, coalescing, scope, exclusion, gap, investigation, and explanation tests plus a local smoke trace.

nodes.title: Add background lifecycle, settings, status, and notifications
nodes.summary: Connect persistent monitoring to launch-at-login, settings and privacy controls, human-readable status/history, threshold notifications, pause/resume, and degraded-state recovery.

acceptance_criteria.description: A user can control launch, roots, exclusions, retention, thresholds, investigation mode, and monitoring pause; the popover explains active, degraded, and recovered states accessibly.

required_evidence.description: Settings/state tests, notification policy tests, SMAppService adapter tests, and reproducible degraded/recovery observations.

nodes.title: Implement complete evidence bundle export
nodes.summary: Export a consistent time-bounded database view into a concise Codex brief, structured summaries, compressed event detail, integrity hashes, limitations, and schema/version metadata.

acceptance_criteria.description: Exports are deterministic for fixtures, consistent under concurrent writes, integrity-verifiable, bounded by requested period, explicit about unknowns, and contain no file contents or unredacted secrets.

required_evidence.description: Golden-bundle tests, schema validation, hash verification, concurrency tests, redaction tests, and a human-readable brief inspection.

nodes.title: Audit persistent evidence recorder increment
nodes.summary: Verify a real monitored-growth journey, retention and privacy bounds, human explanation, notifications, complete export, recovery, and all inherited snapshot behavior.

acceptance_criteria.description: The current build repeats increment one and demonstrates persistent watched-root growth, unexplained growth, threshold handling, export integrity, bounded retention, and restart recovery.

required_evidence.description: Full automated suite, end-to-end fixture trace, UI observations, resource sample, restart test, and inspected evidence bundle.

required_context: All increment-one and increment-two source, tests, and prior gate evidence
